identifier: Markets
statement: You can use Markets to sell to customers in different countries and regions from a single store.

identifier: Understanding markets
statement: Markets group countries, regions, or customer segments into audiences that receive a tailored shopping experience.

identifier: Managing markets and submarkets
statement: After your markets are active, you can create, edit, activate, deactivate, and delete markets as your business grows.

identifier: submarkets
statement: To create more targeted experiences within an existing market, you can use submarkets that inherit their parent market's settings.

identifier: localization

identifier: Overview of markets features and concepts
statement: Each market represents a set of customers, such as those in a particular region, and the customizations you apply to that market determine what experience those customers get when they visit your store.

identifier: Conditions
statement: Conditions: Conditions define who your market applies to. Conditions can be countries and regions for cross-border selling, company locations for B2B, retail locations for selling in person, or sales channels for selling across channels.

identifier: Customizations
statement: Customizations: Customizations define your store experience for the customers in that market, such as available products, pricing, and theme customizations.

identifier: backup region
statement: If a customer doesn't match any of your active markets when browsing the online store, then the experience that they get is that of your backup region instead.

identifier: Cross-border markets
statement: Create markets for countries and regions to sell across borders. You can group countries together, or create single-country markets to target specific regions.

identifier: B2B markets
statement: Create markets for B2B company locations or groups of B2B customers grouped by region, and customize your B2B selling experience based on your negotiated contracts with B2B customers.

identifier: Retail markets
statement: If you have a network of retail locations that offer different products or pricing, then you can customize those experiences with retail markets.

identifier: Channel markets
statement: Create markets for the sales channels that you sell through, and customize product availability, pricing, and currency for each channel. You can group channels to share the same catalog, or give a single channel its own product catalog.

identifier: Sub-region markets
statement: Create markets that target specific states or provinces within a country, so that you can set up different shipping options for different sub-regions. This feature is available as early access.

identifier: Local currencies
statement: Customize your markets to display prices in your customers' local currency with automatic exchange rates.

identifier: Online store customizations
statement: Apply different theme customizations, domains, subfolders, and languages for each of your markets.

identifier: Duties and taxes
statement: Configure tax-inclusive pricing and duty collection for international orders for each market.

identifier: Business entities
statement: If your business has different entities globally, then you can configure markets to use business entities in different global regions.

identifier: Market
statement: A market is a set of customers that you define in your store. Markets can be made up of countries or regions for cross-border sales, company locations for B2B sales, retail locations for in-person sales, or sales channels for selling across channels.

identifier: Market
statement: When you create new markets for the first time, their market customizations inherit your store's default settings. If you create a submarket, then the submarket inherits its customizations from the parent market.

identifier: Market
statement: When a customer visits your store, it's determined which market they belong to, and the experience that you've configured for that market is displayed.

identifier: Submarkets
statement: A submarket is a market that exists within another market. Submarkets inherit the customizations of their parent market, which means you don't need to configure every setting from scratch.

identifier: Catalogs
statement: A catalog is a set of products with optional custom pricing that you assign to a market. Catalogs determine which products are available in each market, and at what price.

identifier: plan requirements
statement: Setting up markets for B2B or retail locations depends on your store's plan, so review the plan requirements.

identifier: B2B markets
statement: On the Basic, Grow, and Advanced plans, you can assign up to 3 active catalogs across all your B2B markets.
scope: Basic, Grow, and Advanced plans

identifier: Retail markets
statement: Customizing catalogs for use with retail markets requires Shopify POS Pro or the Plus plan.

identifier: Business entities
statement: Configuring business entities requires the Plus plan.

identifier: Market
statement: You can override inherited values and customize the following aspects of your store: * Currency * Catalogs (product prices and publishing) * Online store theme customizations * Domain and language settings * Duties and tax settings * Business entities (Shopify Plus only)

identifier: Requirements for using Markets
statement: You need to have shipping rates configured for all countries and regions that you want to sell to. Markets can be activated only for countries and regions that have shipping rates.

identifier: Fixed amount discounts
statement: Fixed amount discounts can be created only in your store's default currency. The discount amount is converted to your customer's currency at checkout based on current exchange rates.

identifier: Staff permissions
statement: Staff permissions can't be assigned per market. For example, if a staff member has the permission to view Orders, then they can view orders in all your store's markets.

identifier: theme
statement: Only one theme can be published at a time. You can customize your theme per market, but customizations must be applied to your published theme.

identifier: Post-purchase apps
statement: Post-purchase apps work only in your store's default currency. Post-purchase offers aren't displayed for customers in markets that use a different currency.

identifier: active market
statement: Only customers from countries or regions in an active market can check out. If you want to sell to customers in a country or region, then it must be included in an active market. B2B company locations, retail locations, and sales channels only need to be included in a market if you want to customize their buying experience.

identifier: Staff permissions for using Markets
statement: To access the Markets page, a staff member needs all of the following permissions: * Home * Orders (all permissions) * Products (all permissions) * Analytics (all permissions) * Discounts (all permissions) * Catalogs (create and edit) * Store settings: manage settings, shipping and delivery, taxes and duties, domains

identifier: Requirements for using Markets
statement: To accept payments in multiple currencies, you need to use Shopify Payments or Adyen as your payment processor. If you use a different payment processor, then customers in all markets pay in your store's default currency.

identifier: Per-market theme customization
statement: Per-market theme customization, such as showing different section content, banners, or layouts for different markets, requires the Advanced plan or higher. On other plans, all markets share the same theme customization.

identifier: Understanding market types
statement: Markets can be created for different types of customers depending on how you sell. Each market type uses a different kind of condition to define its audience.

identifier: Country or region markets
statement: Country or region markets are displayed to customers based on their geographic location. These markets are used for cross-border and international selling.

identifier: Country or region markets
statement: When a customer visits your online store, their location is determined and they're matched to the appropriate country or region market. The customer then receives the experience that you've configured for that market, including currency, language, product availability, and theme customizations. A country or region market can contain a single country or multiple countries.

identifier: Single-country markets
statement: Single-country markets contain one country or region. When you create a single-country market, the currency is automatically set to that country's local currency.

identifier: Multi-country markets
statement: Multi-country markets contain more than one country or region. When you create a multi-country market, the currency customization is set to use local currencies by default. Local currencies are activated so that each country displays prices in its own currency.

identifier: Sub-region markets {#sub-region-markets}
statement: A sub-region market targets a specific state or province, instead of a whole country. Use one when you want different shipping for part of a country.

identifier: Sub-region markets {#sub-region-markets}
statement: On a sub-region market, you can customize only the shipping options. Everything else, such as currency, catalogs, theme, and domain, is inherited from the parent market.

identifier: Retail markets
statement: Retail markets use POS locations as their condition. A retail market can target all POS locations, or specific POS locations. Retail customers are also part of a regional market based on the POS location's address, which means that a retail transaction can be associated with both a retail market and a country or region market.

identifier: B2B markets
statement: You can include company locations in B2B markets in three different ways: * All company locations in all regions: Includes all company locations, regardless of where they're located. * All company locations within a region: Includes all company locations shipping to addresses in the selected regions. As you add more company locations that meet this criteria, they're automatically matched to these markets. * Specific company locations: Includes only the company locations you specify, regardless of where they're shipping to.

identifier: Channel markets
statement: Channel markets use sales channels as their condition. A channel market can contain a single sales channel, or a group of channels sharing the same customizations. Channel markets let you set product availability, pricing, and currency for the specific sales channels that you sell through, such as Google & YouTube, Facebook & Instagram, or TikTok.

identifier: Channel markets
statement: When you create a channel market, the connected sales channels inherit the parent country or region market's catalog and currency by default. You can customize the channel market to set separate product availability, pricing, or currency that meets the channel's own requirements.

identifier: Combining market types
statement: You can use all market types in the same store. Markets of different types can overlap, in which case the customer's experience is based on which settings are the most specific: * B2B markets are more specific than retail markets. Retail markets are more specific than country or region markets. * When a customer qualifies for markets of multiple types, the more specific market type takes priority for how your market customizations take effect. * Catalogs from all applicable markets are combined, so customers can access products from all relevant catalogs.

identifier: Submarkets across market types
statement: When inheriting customizations: * Customizations from the same market type parent are combined. * Customizations from a different market type parent are overridden by the more specific type.

identifier: Country or region market availability
statement: Country or region markets are available on all Shopify plans. There's no limit to the number of country or region markets you can create.

identifier: Sub-region markets {#sub-region-markets}
statement: Sub-region markets are available as an early access feature. Features and functionality might change before general availability.

identifier: Retail markets, Plan requirement
statement: Retail markets are available for all Shopify plans. Customizing catalogs to use with retail markets requires Shopify POS Pro or the Plus plan.

identifier: B2B markets, Plan requirement
statement: On the Basic, Grow, and Advanced plans, you can assign up to 3 active catalogs across all your B2B markets. Assigning 3 catalogs to one B2B market uses the full limit. You need to remove or draft an existing assignment before you can add catalogs to another market. On the Shopify Plus plan, you can create an unlimited number of B2B market catalogs.

identifier: Markets
statement: You can create markets from the Markets page in your Shopify admin to define where and how you sell to different customer groups.

identifier: Review your default markets
statement: When you create a Shopify store, the following markets are created for you automatically: * Domestic market: Your store's home country or region, as determined by your store's address and currency. This is your domestic market and represents the default customer experience. The country in your domestic market is set as your backup region by default. * International market: A curated list of countries or regions where merchants similar to you also sell. This market is inactive by default.

identifier: Create a market {#create-market}, Includes, Add condition
statement: In the Includes section, click Add condition. This condition defines which of your customers the market is displayed to: * To create a Regional market, select Regions, and then select the country or regions to create a market for. * To create a sub-region market, select Regions, open the country you want to target, and then select the states or provinces to create a market for. Learn more about sub-region markets. * To create a B2B market, select Company locations, and then select the company locations to create a market for. To limit the market to one area, use the in filter to display only company locations in a specific region or sub-region, such as a state or province. * To create a Retail market, select POS locations, and then select the retail locations to create a market for. * To create a Channel market, select Channels, and then select the sales channels to create a market for.

identifier: Create a market {#create-market}, Inherited, Customized
statement: In the Inherited section, review the customizations for your new market. These settings are inherited from your store defaults, or from a parent market if the new market has one.

identifier: Activate your market
statement: If you create a market as a draft, or if you don't already ship to all the countries in a new market, then the market is inactive by default. Customers in inactive markets can't complete a purchase, and receive the backup region experience when they visit your store.

identifier: Determining markets
statement: Markets for a customer are automatically determined by using the following information: * When a customer first visits your store, their geographic location is determined by using their IP address, and they're matched to the appropriate market. * The customer's browser language preferences are used to determine which language to display, if you've configured multiple languages for that market. * If a customer arrives on a market-specific domain, subdomain, or subfolder (for example, yourstore.com/fr/), then they get the experience for that market. * If a customer manually chooses a different country or language by using your store's selectors, then their preference is saved and used for future visits.

identifier: Setting up localization for markets
statement: Different countries and regions have different expectations for how prices are displayed. For example, customers in Europe expect tax-inclusive prices, but customers in the United States expect tax to be added during checkout. Showing the wrong format creates confusion.

identifier: Automatic redirection
statement: You can choose whether you want to automatically or manually localize your customers. By default, automatic redirection is activated in new stores, and automatic language detection is deactivated.

identifier: Checkout
statement: A customer's shipping address determines the final experience they receive. For example, if a customer from the United States is shopping online in USD but enters a Canadian shipping address at checkout, then their experience is updated to match the Canada market, including currency and any other customizations that are applied to the Canada market.

identifier: Customize market settings
statement: When you create a market, you can leave settings as inherited from a parent market or from store defaults, or customize them. The following settings can be customized per market: * The currency displayed to customers in this market. * The catalogs that determine the products and pricing available to customers in this market. * Theme customizations specific to this market. * Checkout profile and customer account configuration. * The domain and language used by customers in this market. * Tax-inclusive pricing and duty collection settings. * The shipping options set up for this market.

identifier: Add or remove countries from a market
statement: You can adjust which countries or regions belong to a market as your selling strategy changes. A country or region can be included in more than one market.

identifier: Deactivate a market
statement: If you no longer want to sell to customers in a particular market, then you can deactivate it. Deactivating a market saves all your settings, so you can reactivate it later.

identifier: Delete a market
statement: Deleting a market is permanent. Deleted markets can't be recovered, and must be recreated if needed.

identifier: Change your primary market
statement: Your primary market is the main country or region that you sell to. It's typically your domestic market, and represents the default customer experience for your store. Review the following characteristics of the primary market: * Your primary market can contain only one country or region. * Your primary market can't be deleted. * All changes to your store's default settings apply to your primary market automatically. * Your primary market is determined by your store currency in Settings > General. For example, if your store address is in the United States but your currency is set to Canadian dollars, then your primary market is set to Canada.

identifier: Change your primary market
statement: Markets with subfolders configured can't be made into a primary market, because it would create broken URLs. Update the domain settings first. Markets with more than one region also can't be made primary, because primary markets are limited to one region.

identifier: Parent markets and submarkets
statement: Markets form a hierarchy based on their conditions: * A market with broader conditions is a parent market of a market with more specific conditions. * A market with more specific conditions is a submarket of the broader market.

identifier: Create a submarket
statement: If a new market is determined to be within an existing market, then it's considered a submarket.

identifier: Inheritance rules for submarkets, Currency
statement: Submarkets inherit the currency of their parent market by default. * Customizing the currency on a submarket overrides the parent's currency. If a submarket has multiple parent markets with different currencies, then the currency that best matches the customer's local currency is used. If no currencies match, then the most recently updated customization is prioritized.

identifier: Inheritance rules for submarkets, Catalogs
statement: If the same product exists in both a parent market and submarket catalog at different prices, then the submarket's price is used. If the same product exists in multiple parent catalogs at different prices, then the lowest price is displayed.

identifier: Inheritance rules for submarkets, Domains and languages
statement: If a submarket has multiple parent markets with different domain settings, then it inherits all of them. Customers stay on the same domain throughout their session.

identifier: Inheritance rules for submarkets, Business entity
statement: Submarkets inherit the business entity of their parent market. * Customizing the business entity on a submarket overrides the parent market's setting. If multiple parent markets have different business entities, then they're prioritized in order of creation. The oldest business entity is used.

identifier: Inheritance rules for submarkets, Duties and taxes
statement: If multiple parent markets have different duties and tax settings, then the setting best suited to the customer's location is used.

identifier: Deleting a submarket
statement: After you delete a submarket, customers in the submarket's region receive the parent market experience instead. Other submarkets of the same parent market aren't affected. When you delete a parent market, its submarkets no longer inherit settings from it. The submarkets continue to exist, but their inherited settings revert to your store's defaults.

identifier: Market nodes, Business entity
statement: A market node's business entity section displays the name of the business entity associated with that market.

identifier: channel markets
statement: You can customize only catalogs and currencies for channel markets.

identifier: Market customizations and their effects
statement: Customization What it affects Catalogs Which products are available in the market, and at what price. Local currencies The currency displayed to customers when browsing and paying. Online store Theme sections, blocks, and content displayed to customers in the market. Domains and languages The URL structure and language customers experience. Duties and taxes How taxes are displayed and whether duties are collected at checkout. Business entities Which legal entity processes payments for the market. Shopify Plus only.
note: The table's columns: Customization, What it affects.

identifier: Inheritance
statement: If a market doesn't have a specific customization, then it inherits the value from its parent market. If there's no parent market, then the store default is used.

identifier: Setting up business entities for markets
statement: A business entity is the legal entity that processes payments for orders in a market. If your business has different legal entities in different countries or regions, then you can assign specific business entities to specific markets so that payments are processed through the correct entity.

identifier: Setting up business entities for markets
statement: By default, all orders in your store are processed through your primary Shopify Payments account, which is associated with your store's home country. If you have multiple Shopify Payments accounts for different legal entities in different countries, then you can assign each entity to the appropriate market.

identifier: Setting up business entities for markets
statement: This is important for businesses that need to comply with local payment regulations, simplify tax reporting, or manage payouts in different currencies through local bank accounts.

identifier: Payouts with multiple business entities
statement: When you use multiple business entities, payouts for each entity are deposited into the bank account associated with that entity's Shopify Payments account. Each entity can have its own payout currency and schedule.

identifier: Setting up business entities for markets, Plan requirement
statement: Business entities are available on the Plus plan only.

identifier: Considerations
statement: Business entities are relevant only for stores using Shopify Payments with multiple accounts. * Changing the business entity for a market affects only new orders. Existing orders continue to be associated with the business entity that was active when the order was placed. * If you don't add a business entity customization to a market, then orders in that market are processed through your default Shopify Payments account. * Some regions have regulations about which entity can process payments for customers in that region. Verify with a legal or finance expert that your business entity assignments comply with local requirements.

identifier: Add a business entity customization to a market
statement: Before you can assign business entities to markets, you need to set up additional Shopify Payments accounts for each legal entity.

identifier: Creating catalogs for markets
statement: By default, all the products in your store are available in every market at your store's default prices. When you create a catalog and assign it to a market, you can include or exclude specific products and set custom prices.

identifier: Create a catalog, Set prices in
statement: In the Set prices in field, select the currency for the catalog. Customers browse and pay in the currency of their market, regardless of the catalog currency.

identifier: Product publishing and availability
statement: Products must be included in a catalog assigned to a market for customers in that market to view and purchase them. Product publishing per market applies to your online store's product listings and search results.

identifier: Product publishing and availability
statement: Product publishing rules don't apply to draft orders. You can add any product to a draft order regardless of market restrictions.

statement: From your Shopify admin, go to Markets > Catalogs.

identifier: Assigning domains and languages to markets
statement: A domain and language customization is a combination of a URL structure and a language for a specific market. When a customer visits your store, their location is used to identify their market and direct them to the appropriate domain and language.

identifier: Settings > Languages
statement: Before you can assign a language to a market, the language must be added to your store.

identifier: Translate & Adapt
statement: Beyond translation, the Translate & Adapt app lets you create custom content for specific markets. For example, you can adapt product descriptions, promotional banners, or legal text for different regions, even if those regions share the same language.

identifier: Domain / language
statement: Choose your domain strategy: * Subfolder: Your market is served from a path on your primary domain (for example, yourstore.com/fr/). * Subdomain: Your market is served from a subdomain (for example, fr.yourstore.com). * Separate domain: Your market is served from a different top-level domain (for example, yourstore.fr). The domain must be connected to your Shopify store in Settings > Domains.

identifier: Hreflang tags
statement: Hreflang tags are automatically generated for your store based on your market and language configuration.

identifier: Setting up duties and taxes for markets
statement: Duties and taxes customizations control two things for a market: * Tax display: Whether taxes are displayed as included in the product price or added as a separate line item at checkout. * Duty collection: Whether duties and import taxes are calculated and collected at checkout for international orders.

identifier: Add a duties and taxes customization to a market
statement: To collect sales tax for a market, you must first enter a tax registration for the regions that the market includes.

identifier: Dynamic tax display
statement: Dynamic tax display: Product prices include taxes in regions where appropriate, such as Australia or the European Union. Product prices exclude taxes where appropriate, such as Canada or the United States. Select this option to automatically present prices as your customers would expect.

identifier: Setting up currencies for markets
statement: Each market can have a currency customization that determines what currency is displayed to customers in that market. When a customer visits your store, their market is identified and prices are displayed in the currency configured for that market.

identifier: Currency, exchange rate settings
statement: Select your exchange rate settings: * Select Dynamic to automatically convert prices. Prices are converted using the current market exchange rate, updated regularly. The currency conversion fee is included in the price that's displayed to your customer. * Select Manual to set a fixed exchange rate. The conversion fee isn't added to prices displayed to your customer. Instead, the fee is reflected in your payouts.

identifier: Currency for multi-country markets
statement: If you deactivate local currencies for a multi-country market, then prices in the market's base currency are displayed for all customers in that market, regardless of their location.

identifier: Conversion fees
statement: The currency conversion fee is charged when a customer pays in a currency that's different from your Shopify Payments payout currency. The fee is either 1.5% or 2%, depending on your store's location.

identifier: Currency conversion fee rates based on store location for Shopify Payments merchants.
statement: Store location Conversion fee United States 1.5% United Kingdom, European Economic Area, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and other regions 2%
note: The table's columns: Store location, Conversion fee.

identifier: Fees and multi-entity stores
statement: If your store uses multiple business entities with Shopify Payments accounts in different countries, then the conversion fee depends on which entity processes the payment. If the customer's payment currency matches the entity's payout currency, then no conversion fee is charged.

identifier: Supported currencies
statement: Shopify Payments supports several currencies for international selling. The currencies available to you depend on your store's location and your payment processor. If a country's local currency isn't supported by Shopify Payments, then prices in the market's base currency are displayed to customers in that country instead.

identifier: Considerations for theme customizations
statement: You can customize the following for each market: * Section content such as text, images, or banners * Block visibility and ordering * Section-level settings

identifier: Considerations for theme customizations
statement: The following theme elements can't be customized for your markets on any plan: * Theme settings such as global colors or typography * Liquid templates

identifier: Customizing online store for markets, Plan requirement
statement: Homepage banners, announcement bars, and block content can't differ between markets on the Basic or Grow plans, even if you use the Translate & Adapt app for market-specific wording for the same language.
scope: Basic or Grow plans

identifier: Discount eligibility by market
statement: You can assign discounts to specific B2B, country or region, and retail markets, but you can't assign discounts to specific channel markets. By default, discount codes work across all markets.

identifier: Gift cards
statement: Gift cards are created and denominated in your store's default currency. You can't create gift cards in a specific market's local currency.

identifier: Backup region in Markets
statement: This backup region isn't a market. Instead, it's a setting that points to a country within one of your active markets. The customer experience for the backup region is based on the settings of the market that contains the backup region country.

identifier: Configure your backup region
statement: The backup region must be a country that's contained within an active market. If you deactivate the market that contains your backup region country, then you need to update your backup region to a country in a different active market.

identifier: Settings > General, Backup Region
statement: In the Backup Region section, select the region that you want to display to customers who don't match any existing market.

identifier: Backup region and the domestic market
statement: When you first create your store, your domestic market is created automatically with your home country, and the backup region is set to that same country. This means unmatched customers receive the same experience as your domestic customers, without the ability to complete a checkout.

identifier: Changes to Markets currency customizations with Bulgarian Lev
statement: If you use Shopify Payments, then your markets were previously configured to display and charge customers in Bulgarian Lev. This configuration has been changed to display and charge customers in Euros on your behalf. No other aspects of your customer experience have been changed.

identifier: Dual pricing display requirements with Bulgarian Lev
statement: Between August 8, 2025 and December 31, 2026, all businesses selling to customers in Bulgaria in Euros are required to display prices in both Euros and Bulgarian Lev. Your Shopify checkout is already compliant with this requirement.

identifier: Discount changes {#discount-changes}

identifier: Managed Markets
statement: If you no longer want to use Managed Markets, then you can deactivate it for a specific market or for your entire store.

identifier: merchant of record

identifier: Merchant of record disclaimer at checkout {#mor-disclaimer}
statement: The disclaimer is displayed only to customers in the markets that are managed by Managed Markets. Your domestic checkout remains unchanged.

identifier: Include duties and taxes in prices dynamically by region

identifier: Determining tax on the Managed Markets fee {#fee-tax}
statement: In some countries, the Managed Markets fee is taxable. Whether the fee is taxed depends on the address associated with the legal business name on your store. This address determines both whether tax is added to the fee, and which tax applies: * If your legal business address is in the United States, then no tax is added to the Managed Markets fee. * If your legal business address is in the United Kingdom, then VAT is added to the Managed Markets fee. * If your legal business address is in Canada, then GST, HST, QST, PST, or RST is added to the Managed Markets fee, depending on your province.

identifier: Delivered duty paid (DDP) shipping
statement: Stores in the United States can buy DHL Express, DHL eCommerce, and FedEx labels. Stores in Canada and the United Kingdom can buy DHL Express and FedEx labels.

identifier: Fraud and chargebacks {#fraud}
statement: If your store is based in the United States, then your Managed Markets orders are automatically reviewed for fraud, and eligible orders are protected from fraud chargebacks with Shopify Protect.

identifier: Local payment methods {#local-payment-methods}

identifier: Set a currency for a market in Markets

identifier: International domains, Plan requirement
statement: International domains are available on the Basic Shopify plan or higher.

identifier: Considerations
statement: You can't create international domains from your store's myshopify.com domain. You must use a custom domain, bought through either Shopify or a third-party domain provider.

identifier: Considerations
statement: Some country-specific domains, such as .ca and .fr, have certain residency or business registration requirements that you need to meet when you buy a domain through Shopify.

identifier: Considerations
statement: Language-only subfolders such as /fr or /en can only exist on your primary market. On your secondary markets, subfolders must combine the language code with a country code to display customized content in local languages and currencies. For example, /fr-ca or /en-eu.

identifier: Set up unique URLs for specific countries or regions {#set-up-urls}
statement: By default, only your store's primary language is activated when you create your markets. If you sell in multiple languages and you set up international domains by using subfolders, subdomains, or top-level domains, then you can activate additional languages for each market.

identifier: Set up target markets using your primary domain only
statement: When you set up your markets to use your primary domain only, you don't need to configure any further options in your Shopify admin. Because all markets use the same store URL, you can't customize which languages are available to each market.

identifier: Directing customers to the correct country or region {#directing-customers}
statement: To comply with local legislation, customers from the European Union (EU) aren't automatically redirected within the EU.
scope: customers from the European Union (EU)

identifier: Directing customers to their country or region with deep links {#deep-links}
statement: You can create a parameter that sends customers to the correct country or region using two digit country codes according to ISO 3166 standards.

identifier: Show location and language recommendations to your customers {#show-recommendations}
statement: For example, if your store is based in the United States, then your default country is the United States, where prices are displayed in USD and your default language is English. If you create a market for France that sells in Euros and French, then the Geolocation app recommends that visitors from France select France and the French language to display your store in Euros and French.
note: The page's note says the Geolocation app can no longer be installed and is shut down; its second citation is that note.

identifier: Setting up languages for your store {#managing-languages}
statement: You can then manage your store's languages: add, publish, and remove languages, change your store's default language, and choose the languages that each market uses.

identifier: Pricing in local currencies
statement: You can customize your local pricing for each market by rounding prices. You can also control the prices in different markets using price percentage adjustments, and by setting the product prices by country or region.

identifier: country selector
statement: If you sell in local currencies, then you need to have a country selector so that customers can select their local country or region and your store displays their local currency.

identifier: Shipping zones and markets
statement: Countries and regions can be added to your shipping zones in your Shipping and delivery settings only when those countries and regions belong to a market.

identifier: Shipping options by market
statement: You can set up shipping options for each market that you sell to. A shipping option is a delivery choice that a customer can select at checkout, such as Standard or Express, and each option contains rates that can vary by product and location. You set up and manage shipping options from Markets in your Shopify admin.

identifier: Inherited and customized shipping options
statement: To give a market its own shipping, you customize it, and then set up shipping options that apply only to that market. Customizing a market affects that market and any child markets that inherit from it, but not its parent market or unrelated markets. You can customize shipping for regional and B2B markets.

identifier: Markets permission
statement: Make sure that staff who manage shipping have the Markets permission, because it isn't granted automatically and isn't included in existing staff roles.

identifier: Shipping options by market, Early access
statement: Shipping options by market is in early access and is available only to certain stores.

identifier: Additional address fields
statement: Depending on the country, the following changes are made to the checkout shipping and billing address form: * The Address field in the checkout is replaced by additional fields for Street name and Building number. * An additional Neighborhood field is added. For the following countries and regions, these fields are required. Customers need to complete them before they can proceed with Shopify Checkout. You can't change which additional fields are included or whether a field is required. These additional address fields are displayed only when the customer selects one of the following countries or regions during checkout: * Brazil * Kuwait * Panama * Peru * Philippines

identifier: Additional address fields, Early access
statement: If your store was included in the early access version of this feature, then your checkout still offers additional address fields for the following countries and regions: Belgium, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Germany, Indonesia, Israel, Mexico, Netherlands, Saudi Arabia, Spain, Taiwan, Turkey, United Arab Emirates, and Vietnam.

identifier: Checkout address validation errors
statement: Address validations at checkout, such as state or province and postal code matching, apply to all regions and can't be deactivated unless the store is on the Shopify Plus plan.

identifier: Address format validation, Markets
statement: Optional: In the Markets section, click Add a market to select specific region-based markets. By default, the validation applies to all markets. Only region markets are supported.

identifier: Settings > General
statement: * Business details: Review and manage your legal business entity in this section, such as your store country, business type, phone number, business representatives, and email address. Learn more about managing business entities. * Store contact details: Manage store contact information, such as store name, phone number, email address, and business address. Customers can view this information on your store and policy pages. * Store defaults: Manage your default currency, currency formatting, measurement and weight units, and time zone in this section.

identifier: Change your store address {#change-your-store-address}
statement: Your store address is public, and your customers might view this information on marketing emails, packaging slips, and policy pages. The store address must be in the same country as your business entity address.

identifier: Change your store address {#change-your-store-address}
statement: Changing your store's country might affect the following details: * Your subscription fees and billing currency. * The local language and currency for your store. * Your tax and duty obligations. * Shipping availability. * Your access to Shopify products and services.

identifier: billing address
statement: The company name and address on your Shopify bills come from your billing address, which is a separate setting from your store address. Changing your store address doesn't change your billing address.

identifier: Change your store address {#change-your-store-address}
statement: If your store uses financial services such as Shopify Payments, Shopify Balance, Shopify Capital, or Shopify Credit, then you need to deactivate all financial services before you can change your store's country in your Shopify admin.

identifier: Managing your Shopify billing address
statement: Your billing address is the registered address that you pay Shopify from, and it's the address displayed on your Shopify bills. Your billing address determines the billing taxes that apply to your account, the payment methods and billing currencies that are available to you, and the Shopify company that issues your bill.

identifier: Settings > Billing > Billing profile, Address and currency
statement: You can manage your billing address in the Address and currency section of the Settings > Billing > Billing profile page of your Shopify admin.

identifier: Requirements for your billing address
statement: Your billing address is subject to the following validation rules that don't apply to your store address: * The country of your billing address must match the country of one of your active business entities. You select the entity when you change your address, so you can't enter a country that you don't have an entity in. Learn more about managing business entities. * Your billing currency must be supported for the country of your billing address. If the country that you select doesn't support your current billing currency, then you need to select a supported currency before you can save the address.

identifier: Change your billing address
statement: If your store is on the Shopify Plus plan, then your address and currency are specified by your Shopify Plus contract and you can't change them yourself. To update them, contact Shopify Plus Support.
scope: stores on the Shopify Plus plan

identifier: Pay bills and edit preferences, including payment method
statement: To change your billing address, you need the Pay bills and edit preferences, including payment method organization permission.

identifier: Supported countries and regions for local currency billing {#local-currency-billing-countries}
statement: Local currency billing is available for merchants located in the following countries and regions on all plans: * Australia (AUD) * Canada (CAD) * European Union countries (EUR) * India (INR) * Japan (JPY) * United Kingdom (GBP) Billing in EUR is also available in Liechtenstein and Switzerland. Local currency billing is available for merchants located in the following countries and regions, and isn't available for the Plus plan: * Czech Republic (CZK) * Denmark (DKK) * Liechtenstein (CHF) * Norway (NOK) * Poland (PLN) * Romania (RON) * Singapore (SGD) * Sweden (SEK) * Switzerland (CHF) For all other countries and regions, Shopify bills are issued in USD.

identifier: Change your billing currency
statement: The billing currencies that are available to you are determined by the country of your billing address.

identifier: Requirements for using Managed Markets
statement: Your store currency must be the default currency of the country where your business is based. For example, a business that's based in the United States needs a store currency of USD. If your store currency is different, then you can't activate Managed Markets.

identifier: Requirements for using Managed Markets
statement: Your store and product information need to be available in English. English can be your default language, or you can add and publish English as an additional language. Translate your product titles and descriptions into English.

identifier: Requirements for using Managed Markets
statement: In addition to meeting these requirements, there are requirements for Managed Markets specific to where your business is based.

identifier: Requirements for using Managed Markets in the United States
statement: To use Managed Markets in the United States, you need to meet the following requirements: * Your business needs to be based in the continental United States (exclusive of territories including Puerto Rico and Guam). * Your business needs at least one non-PO box location in the United States. * You need at least one fulfillment location in the continental United States.
scope: United States

identifier: Requirements for using Managed Markets in Canada
statement: To use Managed Markets in Canada, you need to meet the following requirements: * Your business needs to be based in Canada. * Your business needs at least one non-PO box location in Canada. * You need at least one fulfillment location in Canada. * If you have multiple fulfillment locations in Canada, then all your fulfillment locations must be located within the same province. * Your store must use Shopify Tax or Basic Tax. Managed Markets can't be used if your store uses manual tax settings.
scope: Canada

identifier: Requirements for using Managed Markets in the United Kingdom
statement: To use Managed Markets in the United Kingdom, you need to meet the following requirements: * Your business needs to be based in the United Kingdom. * Your business needs at least one non-PO box location in the United Kingdom. * You need at least one fulfillment location in the United Kingdom. * If you have multiple fulfillment locations in the United Kingdom, then all your fulfillment locations must be located either within Great Britain or Northern Ireland. If you have fulfillment locations in both Great Britain and Northern Ireland, then you can't use Managed Markets.
scope: United Kingdom

identifier: Managed Markets country requirements
statement: Managed Markets collects duties and import taxes at checkout using delivered duty paid (DDP) in every country and region where DDP is supported. Your customers pay at checkout instead of paying the carrier or customs on delivery. Delivered duty unpaid (DDU) shipping remains available only in countries and regions where DDP isn't supported.

identifier: Managed Markets country requirements
statement: To keep your customers in a DDP-supported market paying duties on delivery, deactivate Managed Markets for that market.

identifier: Managed Markets feature limitations
statement: Managed Markets doesn't support multiple business entities in a single store.

identifier: Managed Markets feature limitations
statement: B2B orders aren't supported by Managed Markets. You need to act as your own merchant of record for B2B orders.

identifier: EU right of withdrawal in Managed Markets
statement: Managed Markets automatically applies compliant cancellation and return policies to orders from customers in the European Union.
scope: European Union

identifier: EU right of withdrawal in Managed Markets
statement: If you already use a compliant third-party solution, then you can deactivate the Managed Markets right of withdrawal feature and manage your EU compliance independently. This setting is in your admin at Settings > Customer accounts, and requires you to agree to use your own solution for returns and cancellations for Managed Markets in the European Union.
scope: European Union

statement: Receive payouts in USD for stores based in the United States, CAD for stores based in Canada, and GBP for stores based in the United Kingdom.
scope: Managed Markets

identifier: Managed Markets comparison table: Cross-border payments
statement: Use Shopify Payments for domestic transactions and Managed Markets for international transactions.
scope: Managed Markets

statement: Tax inclusive pricing is set for countries where this is standard and local country regulations are handled for you. Manage tax inclusive pricing per individual market.

identifier: Managed Markets changes to your store: Store
statement: Your product catalog is automatically classified with Harmonized System (HS) codes and adjusted for restrictions by country.

identifier: Managed Markets changes to your store: Checkout
statement: Shipping with prepaid duties is used at checkout. In the United States, shipping is available with DHL Express, DHL eCommerce, UPS, and FedEx. In the United Kingdom and Canada, shipping is available with DHL Express and FedEx.

identifier: Managed Markets changes to your store: International sales tools
statement: Incompatible countries are removed. Markets managed by Managed Markets can use only compatible currencies. Review your currency settings before you activate Managed Markets.

identifier: Managed Markets changes to your store: Payments
statement: Managed Markets becomes your merchant of record for international orders in selected markets.

identifier: Activate Managed Markets: self-billing agreement
statement: If your store is based in the United Kingdom or Canada, then you need to sign a self-billing agreement when you activate Managed Markets. A self-billing agreement is required for tax compliance.
scope: United Kingdom; Canada

identifier: Activate Managed Markets
statement: You can activate Managed Markets directly from the Markets page in your Shopify admin. After you complete the activation steps, Managed Markets is immediately active for your selected markets.

identifier: Rest of World
statement: Review the new market created for Managed Markets. By default, this market is called Rest of World and includes all regions that are eligible for Managed Markets, but you can change your market name and remove countries and regions from the list of included regions.

identifier: Deactivate Managed Markets for a specific market
statement: You can remove Managed Markets as the merchant of record for an individual market while keeping it active for your other markets. This lets you self-manage a particular market without affecting the rest of your store's international setup.

identifier: What changes after you deactivate Managed Markets: Merchant of record
statement: Merchant of record: Markets that you deactivate will no longer use Managed Markets as a merchant of record. You become responsible for tax compliance and regulatory requirements in those markets.

identifier: What changes after you deactivate Managed Markets: Shipping rates
statement: Shipping rates: Shipping rates that are exclusive to Managed Markets will no longer be available for the affected markets. In countries or regions that don't have other rates configured, carrier-calculated rates will be added automatically.

identifier: What changes after you deactivate Managed Markets: Duties and import taxes
statement: Duties and import taxes: Managed Markets will no longer calculate duties and import taxes for affected markets. If you want to continue collecting duties and import tax at checkout, make sure you set up Shopify's Duties and import taxes feature once you turn off Managed Markets.

identifier: Managed Markets for Canada
statement: Managed Markets is available for stores based in Canada.
scope: Canada

identifier: Considerations for using Managed Markets in Canada
statement: The following features aren't yet available for Managed Markets in Canada: * Shopify Protect. * Multi-currency payouts. * Refunds for Managed Markets orders.
scope: Canada

identifier: Shipping carriers and fulfillment for Managed Markets in Canada
statement: You can purchase DHL Express and FedEx shipping labels for Managed Markets orders in Canada. Canada Post, DHL eCommerce, and UPS aren't available.
scope: Canada

identifier: Shipping carriers and fulfillment for Managed Markets in Canada
statement: Shipping labels purchased through Managed Markets in Canada are zero-rated. You aren't charged tax on the cost of your Managed Markets shipping labels.
scope: Canada

identifier: Payouts and fees for Managed Markets in Canada: Fees
statement: GST, HST, QST, PST, or RST is added to the Managed Markets fee for stores based in Canada, depending on your province.
scope: Canada

identifier: Merchant of record fee invoices
statement: When you activate Managed Markets, Global-e becomes your merchant of record for international Managed Markets orders. In Canada, you're charged a merchant of record service fee directly.
scope: Canada

identifier: Managed Markets tax invoices for Canada
statement: A Managed Markets order in Canada is considered a business-to-business (B2B) sale from your store to Global-e, who then sells to your customer as the merchant of record. As a result, Managed Markets sales in Canada have tax implications. In Canada, GST, HST, QST, PST, or RST applies to orders, depending on your province.
scope: Canada

identifier: Tax ID validation
statement: In Canada, your GST or HST tax ID is validated, along with your business name. Your GST or HST registration must match your registered legal business name. If your tax registration is invalid or doesn't match your legal business name, then you might be liable for the tax due on your Managed Markets sales.
scope: Canada

identifier: Managed Markets for the United Kingdom
statement: Managed Markets is available for stores based in the United Kingdom.
scope: United Kingdom

identifier: Considerations for using Managed Markets in the United Kingdom
statement: The following features aren't yet available for Managed Markets in the United Kingdom: * Shopify Protect. * Multi-currency payouts. * Refunds for Managed Markets orders.
scope: United Kingdom

identifier: Shipping carriers and fulfillment for Managed Markets in the United Kingdom
statement: You can purchase DHL Express and FedEx shipping labels for Managed Markets orders in the United Kingdom. DHL eCommerce and UPS aren't available.
scope: United Kingdom

identifier: Shipping carriers and fulfillment for Managed Markets in the United Kingdom
statement: Shipping labels purchased through Managed Markets in the United Kingdom are zero-rated. You aren't charged tax on the cost of your Managed Markets shipping labels.
scope: United Kingdom

identifier: Payouts and fees for Managed Markets in the United Kingdom: Fees
statement: VAT is added to the Managed Markets fee for stores based in the United Kingdom.
scope: United Kingdom

identifier: Merchant of record fee invoices
statement: When you activate Managed Markets, Global-e becomes your merchant of record for international Managed Markets orders. In the United Kingdom, you're charged a merchant of record service fee directly.
scope: United Kingdom

identifier: Managed Markets tax invoices for the United Kingdom
statement: A Managed Markets order in the United Kingdom is considered a business-to-business (B2B) sale from your store to Global-e, who then sells to your customer as the merchant of record. As a result, Managed Markets sales in the United Kingdom have tax implications. In the United Kingdom, VAT applies to orders.
scope: United Kingdom

identifier: Tax ID validation
statement: In the United Kingdom, your VAT tax ID and business name are validated. Your VAT registration must be valid and match your registered legal business name. If your VAT registration is invalid or doesn't match your legal business name, then you might be liable for 20% VAT due on your Managed Markets sales.
scope: United Kingdom

identifier: Payouts and fees for Managed Markets: Fees
statement: Managed Markets has the following fees for international orders: * A Shopify Payments processing fee, which varies by your Shopify plan and the payment method used by your customer. * A Managed Markets transaction fee of 3.25% for stores on the Shopify Plus plan, or 3.5% for stores on the Basic, Grow, or Advanced plan. * A currency conversion fee that's the same as the foreign exchange (FX) fee for Shopify Payments in your region.
scope: Canada; United Kingdom

identifier: Review your products
statement: Your products are reviewed before you activate Managed Markets to ensure that they're not prohibited items in the countries and regions that you sell to.

identifier: Set up shipping: flat shipping rates from Managed Markets
statement: You can use flat shipping rates from Managed Markets instead of rates that you set up yourself. This feature is in early access, and is available only to certain merchants. If you have access, then you turn on flat rates for each of your managed markets.

identifier: International pricing for Managed Markets
statement: Including duties and taxes in prices is turned on by default when you activate Managed Markets. You can manage it from the Markets page in your Shopify admin by selecting a market and then selecting Taxes and duties. If you turn it off, then you're responsible for how duties, taxes, and pricing are handled for that market.

identifier: Customer experience with international prices for Managed Markets
statement: For tax-exclusive countries such as Canada, tax is displayed as a separate line at checkout. For tax-inclusive countries, tax is included in the price and no separate line is added.

identifier: How duties and taxes are estimated and guaranteed
statement: The included duties and taxes are calculated as an average for each destination country, not as a single average across all countries.

identifier: Deciding when to include duties and taxes in prices
statement: Including duties and taxes in prices requires local currencies at their guaranteed exchange rate, so it can't be combined with a manual exchange rate for a market. To adjust your prices for a specific country, use catalog price adjustments instead of a manual exchange rate.

identifier: Deactivate duties and taxes in prices for Managed Markets
statement: If you want to manage a market's pricing manually, then you can turn off duties and taxes in prices at any time. After you turn it off, you can choose whether duty and taxes are added in checkout or assumed to be included in your prices.

identifier: Getting paid
statement: The length of time between the date that a customer's payment is captured and the date that your payout is sent to your bank account depends on the country that your store is based in.
scope: Managed Markets

identifier: Prohibited and restricted items on Managed Markets
statement: If you sell a product that's prohibited in a destination country, then Managed Markets hides the product from the catalog for customers in that country.

identifier: Materials depicting illegal acts
statement: Products that depict or endorse illegal activities, either in the country where you operate or the countries that you sell to, are restricted on Managed Markets.

identifier: Subscription products
statement: If you have products set up for subscriptions on your store, then the subscription selling plan is removed for all international markets managed by Managed Markets. Your customers can still buy products as a one-time purchase.

identifier: Review status for Managed Markets products
statement: Products that are in unsupported status for a particular market can't be displayed for customers in that market.

identifier: Managing Managed Markets draft orders
statement: When you create a draft order and add a customer that has a shipping address from a market managed by Managed Markets, then the Managed Markets merchant of record is automatically selected for your draft order.

identifier: Available shipping services with Managed Markets
statement: The shipping labels that you can purchase through Managed Markets depend on where your business is based: * If your business is based in the United States, then you can purchase only DHL eCommerce, DHL Express, FedEx, or UPS shipping labels. * If your business is based in Canada or the United Kingdom, then you can purchase only DHL Express or FedEx shipping labels.
scope: United States; Canada; United Kingdom

identifier: Fulfillment for Managed Market orders
statement: Shipping with Managed Markets is available only from fulfillment locations in a country or region where Managed Markets is supported.

identifier: Peak season surcharges
statement: If your business is based in Canada or the United Kingdom, then the surcharge is waived on all of your Managed Markets labels, because DHL eCommerce and UPS labels are available only to businesses based in the United States.
scope: Canada; United Kingdom; United States

identifier: Flat shipping rates from Managed Markets
statement: Flat shipping rates from Managed Markets are set for each destination and shipping option, so you don't set up or maintain international rates yourself.

identifier: Considerations for using flat shipping rates from Managed Markets
statement: Flat rates are available only for markets where duties and taxes are included in your prices. If you turn off duties and taxes in prices for a market, then flat rates are turned off for that market too.

identifier: Considerations for using flat shipping rates from Managed Markets
statement: The shipping options available to your customers depend on their destination, such as Standard or Express at checkout. The Shipping options row in your market's Shopify Managed Markets settings lists the options for that market.

identifier: Manage flat rates from Managed Markets
statement: You can manage flat rates from Managed Markets for a market. You can also absorb a set amount of the shipping cost on orders above a minimum value. The amount is set for each market and can't be changed, but you can turn it on or off at any time.

identifier: B2B and Markets
statement: Previously, markets were composed only of specific countries or regions. Markets have now been expanded, and can be used to represent specific sets of customers by creating markets and submarkets. You can group your B2B customers to create a customized store experience for each group. For each market, you can customize currency, theme, collection of taxes and duties, discounts, and pricing and product availability with catalogs.

identifier: B2B and Markets, Tip
statement: If your store is on the Shopify Plus plan, then you can activate the new Markets functionality by using feature test drive.
scope: Shopify Plus
note: the same tip on b2b/markets.md and b2b/markets/managing.md

identifier: B2B and Markets, Plan requirement
statement: On the Basic, Grow, and Advanced plans, you can assign up to 3 active catalogs across all your B2B markets. Direct catalog assignment to company locations and unlimited catalogs are available only on the Shopify Plus plan. Theme editor customizations by market are available only on the Advanced plan and higher.
note: b2b/markets/managing.md holds the same note with 'Direct assignment of catalogs to company locations'; S02-SH-083 and S02-SH-114 hold its first sentence from other pages

identifier: B2B All
statement: The following changes are made to your store when you opt in: * A B2B All market is automatically created that includes all your existing companies and locations. * Catalogs aren't assigned to the B2B All market. * Your store's default products, prices, and currency are displayed to companies and company locations outside other markets that don't have an assigned catalog.

identifier: Customer experience determination in B2B with Markets
statement: The experience that a company location receives on your online store is determined by the markets that they match.

identifier: Customer experience determination in B2B with Markets
statement: A company location can match multiple markets at the same time, and which markets they match depends on the shipping address.

identifier: backup region
statement: If a company doesn't match any markets, then your store's backup region is used to determine the customer's experience.

identifier: Creating a market (B2B)
statement: You can create a new market to use with B2B in your Shopify admin on the Markets page. When you create your market, ensure that you select Company locations in the Includes section. To create a functioning B2B market, you must assign company locations to the market. A B2B market without company locations won't deliver B2B pricing or experiences to your wholesale customers.

identifier: Customizing a market (B2B)
statement: After you create your market, you can customize it to best suit your needs. Review the following list to learn more about customizing your market: * Currency * Catalogs * Online store theme * Checkout and accounts configuration * Duties and taxes * Discounts

identifier: Retail markets
statement: Retail markets are a type of market that are designed to support unique customizations for in-person selling with Shopify POS. With Retail markets, you can create retail-specific merchandizing strategies that are different from your online or B2B customer experiences.

identifier: Sales channels and Markets
statement: You can use Markets to set your product availability, pricing, and currency for specific sales channels that you use. You can group channels together in a market, for example using the same shared product catalog for all your social channels, or you can have a single market and product catalog for one specific sales channel.

identifier: Considerations and limitations for using channel markets
statement: * When you create a channel market: * Any regions that you select for the channel market must correspond to regions that are supported by the relevant sales channel. * Any currency that you set in a customized product catalog for the channel market should be the preferred currency for the relevant sales channel. If you set a currency that's not a preferred currency for the sales channel, then a warning message is displayed. * Agentic storefronts sales channels can't be added to channel markets.

identifier: Traffic-generating channels
statement: This means that when you include products in a channel market's catalog for traffic-generating channels, the products must be published to your online store and they need to have the same pricing as your online store. If you try to apply custom catalog pricing to a market for a traffic-generating channel, then a warning message is displayed.

identifier: Order-generating channels
statement: This means that when you include products in a channel market's catalog for order-generating channels, you can choose to set product pricing and availability that's different and separate from what you have in your online store.

identifier: Local currency on orders and draft orders with Markets
statement: When using Markets for international sales, the local currency and pricing are determined by the market associated with the customer's order. The market that's associated with the order, as well as the taxes and duties, are determined by the shipping address of the customer.

identifier: Local currency on orders and draft orders with Markets
statement: Taxes can be included or excluded from item prices, depending on location. For example, orders with the United States market exclude taxes from prices, but orders with the Germany market include taxes in prices. * Tax rates vary by market. At checkout, if a customer changes the shipping address to an address that's outside the market, then the correct tax rate for the customer’s shipping address is charged. The market on the order, with its tax included or excluded setting, is unchanged.

identifier: Selling in multiple currencies with Markets
statement: To sell in multiple currencies using B2B, you must use Shopify Payments.

identifier: Selling in multiple currencies with Markets
statement: The currency set in your catalogs doesn't impact what's displayed to customers in the online store, cart, checkout, or draft orders. The currency is always the market currency either for the markets they match, or the backup region currency if they don't match a market.

identifier: Selling in multiple currencies with Markets
statement: By default, a market's currency is set to the currency for the region that you've selected for your market. You can also select which currency you want to apply to a market, and the prices in your online store, cart, checkout, and draft orders are displayed in the currency that's configured for your customer based on their shipping address.

identifier: Selling in multiple currencies with Markets
statement: When creating or customizing a market, you can choose to use automatic currency conversion or set a rate manually, and determine whether rounding is applied for currency conversion.

identifier: Creating and managing B2B catalogs with Markets
statement: After you create a B2B catalog, you can assign it to a market or a company location to let B2B customers purchase products at specific prices. Assigning a catalog to markets helps you to manage pricing and product availability for all your B2B customers, or groups of company locations.

identifier: Create a catalog with Markets
statement: Each company location can have a maximum of 25 catalogs assigned to it. This limit includes catalogs that are assigned using a market and catalogs that are directly assigned to the company location.

identifier: Considerations for choosing how to assign a catalog
statement: You will not be able to add region catalogs or catalogs that are directly assigned to company locations to a B2B market.

identifier: Additional tax fields in checkout (International shipping considerations)
statement: If you sell to customers in certain countries and regions, then the checkout might display additional required fields. Refer to Countries and regions with additional tax fields for details on the relevant countries and checkout scenarios. These fields are displayed after the customer enters a complete, valid shipping address, grouped with the payment details in a section titled Additional Information. Selecting a country or region alone doesn't display the fields. Customers in these countries and regions enter additional information in these fields. If your customer is a foreign national without the information specific to residents of a particular country or region, then they can enter their passport number in these fields, with the following exceptions: * Brazil: Customers must enter a valid Cadastro de Pessoas Físicas (CPF) or Cadastro Nacional da Pessoa Jurídica (CNPJ) number. Passport numbers aren't accepted. * Italy: The CF field accepts only a Codice Fiscale. The field is optional, so customers without one can leave it blank. After a customer places an order, the additional information is displayed on the order details page.

identifier: Marketing opt-in: Email, customer regions with the consent checkbox preselected (Editing the checkout form options)
statement: The Marketing opt-in section determines how marketing consent is displayed to customers during checkout and sign-in. You can activate the following options: * Email: You can choose whether the marketing consent checkbox appears on checkout, sign-in, or both checkout and sign-in. You can also choose which customer regions have the email marketing consent checkbox preselected during checkout and sign-in. Activating preselected email marketing consent means that the customer has to manually opt out of email marketing during checkout and sign-in by deselecting the consent checkbox. * Regions recommended by Shopify: Customer regions with the email marketing consent checkbox preselected are chosen based on the latest recommendations from Shopify. These automatic recommendations don't constitute legal advice, and you're responsible for complying with your local laws and regulations. * Regions you choose: You can manually choose the customer regions where the email marketing consent checkbox is preselected. You can leave no regions selected so that all customers in all regions must manually opt in to email marketing.

identifier: Shopify B2B features by plan
statement: You can use Shopify B2B on the Basic, Grow, Advanced, and Shopify Plus plans. Shopify B2B isn't available on the Starter or Retail plans. The features available to you depend on your plan. Most B2B features are available on all plans, including companies, catalogs, net payment terms, self-serve ordering, and Shopify Flow automations. Review the following key differences between plans: * B2B market catalogs: On the Basic, Grow, and Advanced plans, you can assign up to 3 active catalogs across all your B2B markets. Assigning 3 catalogs to one B2B market uses the full limit. You need to remove or draft an existing assignment before you can add catalogs to another market. On the Shopify Plus plan, you can create an unlimited number of B2B market catalogs. * Direct company catalogs: On the Shopify Plus plan, you can also assign catalogs directly to specific companies and company locations for customer-level pricing. Direct catalog assignment isn't available on the Basic, Grow, or Advanced plans. * Advanced payments: Deposit requirements, partial payments, and payment requests per fulfillment are available only on the Shopify Plus plan. * Contextual experiences: Contextual checkout and storefront customization through Shopify Markets are available on the Advanced and Plus plans. To use B2B catalog features on the Basic, Grow, or Advanced plans, your store must be using new Shopify Markets.

identifier: Understanding customer privacy settings in your Shopify Admin: region picker cards

identifier: Add a cookie banner {#add-a-cookie-banner}: automated settings, Regions and content
statement: When you set up a new store, automated privacy settings are activated by default, which means we will automatically configure your cookie banner for visitors in the UK and EEA regions, if you have active markets in these regions. However, you can deactivate Use automated settings to manually draft your cookie banner. The Shopify cookie banner may be displayed on storefront, cart, and checkout and customer account pages to visitors in configured regions. Steps: 1. From your Shopify admin, go to Settings > Customer privacy. 2. Click Cookie banner. 3. In the Regions and content section, choose between automated settings or manual customization: * To use automated settings, make sure that the Use automated settings button is activated. If it's not, then activate it using the toggle. This option ensures that your settings remain aligned with Shopify's latest recommendations for regions and content. * For manual region customization, click Edit in the Regions section, select the regions where the cookie banner should display, click Done, and then click Save.

identifier: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
statement: The European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) imposes obligations and responsibilities with respect to personal data for businesses located in or offering goods or services to individuals in the European Economic Area, and Switzerland and the United Kingdom have adopted equivalent laws for UK and Swiss businesses and residents. By using Shopify, there are tools and information that you can use to help you to analyze your business practices and help ensure that you comply with your GDPR obligations. Using services offered by Shopify alone doesn't guarantee that you comply with GDPR. You're generally the controller of your customers’ data. This means that you choose how your customers’ data is handled. If you make goods and services available to individuals in Europe, even if you or your business aren't located in Europe, then GDPR might apply to your business.

identifier: Locations
statement: You can add and manage locations where you store or sell products, such as warehouses, retail stores, or pop-ups. statement: You can add, deactivate, reactivate, and delete your locations from the Locations settings in your Shopify admin. identifier: Location quantity limit {#location-limit}: apps treated as locations

identifier: Add a location {#create-and-modify-locations}
statement: You can add a location in your Shopify admin. Your inventory is made available for online purchases by default in each new location. After you create a location, you can activate delivery methods for your location. Your new location is added to the bottom of your order routing list.

identifier: Location quantity limit {#location-limit}
statement: The maximum number of active locations that you can have depends on your store's Shopify subscription plan. identifier: Order routing (Settings > Shipping and delivery)
statement: You can set up order routing to automatically assign orders to fulfillment locations based on configured rules. Order routing applies rules in sequence to prioritize locations and determine where to fulfill each order. Order routing requires 2 or more active locations. The default order routing strategy includes rules to do the following: * Minimize split fulfillments by choosing locations that can fulfill all items * Stay within the destination market when possible * Ship from the closest location to reduce delivery times
note: found for S02-VP-78 (searches L1 and L2)

identifier: Understanding order routing: default rules
statement: By default, rules are configured to optimize for fulfillment from the closest location within the destination market that has all of the items in the order in stock. There's no need to modify your order routing settings if the default settings work for your business.

identifier: Requirements for country compliance {#requirements}
statement: To remain compliant with country requirements when making in-person sales, your business must meet the following criteria: * Your Shopify store's country must match the country of all your physical stores' locations. * Your Shopify store currency must match the local currency of your physical stores' locations. * Your store's currency must match your Shopify Payments payout bank account currency. identifier: Changing the language of your email templates
statement: The default language that your email templates display in depends on your theme's language and any edits that you've made to the templates: * If you've made no changes to your email templates, then when you change your theme's language, the email template language also changes. * If you've made changes to both the body and title of your email templates, then changing your theme's language doesn't change the language of the email templates. * If you've made changes only to the title of your email templates, then changing your theme's language doesn't change the language of the email templates. * If you've made changes only to the body of your email templates, then changing your theme's language changes the title to the new language but doesn't change the language of the body of your email templates.

identifier: Add a tax registration number to the invoice: countries and regions

In Australia, Canada, and India, businesses that charge the goods and services tax (GST) might need to include their registration number. In the European Union, you might need to include your value added tax (VAT) identification number.

identifier: Setting up your email: Sender email (Settings > Notifications)
statement: Your Sender email is the customer-facing address that's listed in Settings > Notifications and is used in the following ways: * As the email address where your customers can contact you directly. * As the From email address when your customers receive automatic notification emails, order confirmation emails, and any marketing emails sent from your store. * As the address where contact form submissions from your online store are delivered.
